policy_title: Toughen Sentencing for Domestic Murders and 'Rough Sex' Defence
stated: The Conservative Party will toughen sentencing for murders within the context of domestic abuse with new aggravating factors and introduce a 25-year prison term, regardless of weapon use. They will also introduce an aggravating factor for murders in the context of 'rough sex' to prevent it being used as an excuse for lighter sentences.

source.quote: We will toughen sentencing for murders that take place within the context of domestic abuse with new aggravating factors, such as if they involve coercive and controlling behaviour or gratuitous attacks. We will introduce a 25-year prison term for domestic murders, regardless of whether a weapon is used. ...We will introduce an aggravating factor for murders that happen in the context of ‘rough sex’, so it is never used as an excuse to get a lighter sentence.

bearing_set.reason: Directly addresses sentencing for domestic murders and 'rough sex' killings, affecting justice outcomes, deterrence, and victim protection within the criminal justice system.

Closing the 'rough sex' defence loophole and adding aggravating factors for domestic abuse murders materially strengthens equal treatment and due process protections, particularly for women as a class of victims.

membership_note: Two clean bearings: O5 for the justice/sentencing effect on serious crime, O9 for the equal-treatment dimension of gender-based homicide proceedings. O10 (bodily autonomy) was considered but does not clear the bar — the policy restricts a courtroom defence for murder, not consensual conduct itself. O12 (prison costs) was considered but the marginal fiscal effect of longer sentences in a small category of cases is negligible at the policy level.
